claims.headline: Dental pulp stem cells delivered in a GelMA hydrogel were reported to regenerate pulp-like tissue in a rodent model
claims.summary: Tufts researchers encapsulated human dental pulp stem cells and endothelial cells in gelatin methacrylate and delivered them into tooth root segments tested in a rodent model. Pulp-like tissue formed. They called for larger animal studies before human trials.

claims.headline: An injectable self-assembling peptide hydrogel was reported to stimulate dental pulp stem cells after root canal
claims.summary: New Jersey Institute of Technology researchers presented a peptide hydrogel, liquid when injected, meant to stimulate new blood vessels and dental pulp inside a treated tooth. Tests in dogs were under way, with human studies planned if they succeeded.
claims.indication: Pulp loss after root canal treatment

claims.headline: A coronary sinus reducer implant was reported to cut chest pain significantly in three quarters of patients with refractory angina
claims.summary: A study of the coronary sinus reducer, an implant fitted at the Royal Brompton hospital, found a significant fall in chest pain in 75% of patients. One patient fitted in 2021 went from five attacks a week to one every week or two. The article says further trials and NHS approval are still needed.

claims.headline: Light-curable synthetic filling materials were reported to prompt tooth stem cells to regenerate dentine
claims.summary: University of Nottingham and Wyss Institute researchers designed synthetic biomaterials, placed like fillings in direct contact with pulp, to stimulate native stem cells to repair pulp and dentine. The work won a Royal Society of Chemistry prize in 2016.
claims.indication: Pulp and dentine damage from decay

claims.headline: The once-weekly nasal spray INNA-051 was reported to prime the nose's antiviral defences against colds, flu, RSV and coronaviruses
claims.summary: ENA Respiratory's dry-powder nasal spray is designed to prime the nose's own antiviral defences instead of targeting one virus, and the US Department of Defense has put nearly US$10 million into it. The company says it lowers viral load and does not block infection. A Phase 2a community study is under way in the USA.

claims.headline: An optogenetic gene therapy used with light-stimulating goggles was reported to improve light sensitivity in some blind patients with retinitis pigmentosa
claims.summary: In a study published in the New England Journal of Medicine and led by the University of Pittsburgh, ten legally blind adults each received one injection of an algae-derived light-sensing gene in one eye and then wore camera goggles. Light sensitivity improved in several of them and some could find and touch objects. None regained normal sight.

claims.summary: US company Immorta Bio said its experimental peptide SenoMune-0257 is designed to help the immune system find and remove senescent cells, and that planned preclinical studies are complete. The article notes that safety and effectiveness in people have not been established.

claims.headline: Orforglipron was reported to help adults with overweight or obesity and obstructive sleep apnoea in two trials
claims.summary: The Daily Mail reported two clinical trials involving 712 adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea and a BMI of 27 or above, which found the once-daily pill orforglipron could be another treatment option alongside CPAP machines. The article notes the drug was approved by UK officials in August for weight management and type 2 diabetes but is not yet approved for sleep apnoea. A researcher quoted says it could be promising if approved for this use.

claims.summary: Matricelf, a company using technology developed at Tel Aviv University, and Loewenstein Rehabilitation Medical Center announced that they are preparing for a possible first implant of an engineered spinal cord tissue made from a patient's own cells. claims.headline: CAR-T cell therapy was reported to restore function in some people with stiff person syndrome in an early study
claims.summary: Mayo Clinic neurologists gave CAR-T cell therapy, a treatment already used in cancer, to people with stiff person syndrome in an early study published in JAMA Neurology. Some patients who had needed help with daily tasks regained function and returned to work. The researchers say it is not yet known whether the gains last.

claims.summary: University of Oregon biologists rebuilt antimicrobial peptides from extinct mammal ancestors and tested them in the laboratory. Some were more potent against drug-resistant bacteria than the versions humans make today. The researchers present them as clues for designing treatments, not as a treatment.

articles.title: 160-million-year-old proteins show surprising power against superbugs

claims.headline: An antibody blocking the CXCR3 protein was reported to preserve about 40% more memory-centre tissue in mice with tau build-up
claims.summary: Washington University in St. Louis researchers used an antibody against CXCR3, a protein that helps T cells enter the brain, in mice with tau accumulation. Treated mice kept roughly 40% more tissue in memory centres and did better on memory tests, although tau itself was not removed. The work has been done only in mice.

claims.summary: Researchers at Kyoto University and the University of Fukui reported that one dose of an antibody blocking the protein USAG-1 grew a whole new tooth in mice with congenital tooth agenesis, with similar results in ferrets. The paper appeared in Science Advances in February 2021.

claims.summary: Researchers in Shanghai engineered a probiotic strain of E. coli to make the hormone GLP-1 only when blood sugar is high. Taken by mouth, it worked in mice and in diabetic macaques with no sign of harm. The article says trials in people are some way off.

claims.summary: ETH Zurich researchers reported in Science that their implant brought blood sugar back to normal in diabetic, obese mice within 60 to 90 minutes of being switched on, and the animals lost up to 10% of body weight over six weeks. claims.headline: A molecule made by click chemistry was reported to restore vancomycin's ability to kill a drug-resistant superbug
claims.summary: Chemists at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory reported that one of their click-chemistry molecules, made for an unrelated project, let the old antibiotic vancomycin kill vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium again in laboratory tests. The work is at the laboratory stage.

claims.headline: Bioengineered tooth germs transplanted into dogs' jaws were reported to grow into functional teeth
claims.summary: Okayama University researchers reconstructed tooth germs from a beagle's own tooth germ cells and transplanted them into its jaw, where teeth erupted. They suggested immature wisdom tooth germs as a possible cell source in people.
